newsitem.title: INDIA: India VSNL awaits elusive government nod.
newsitem.headline: India VSNL awaits elusive government nod.

text.p: A controversial equity issue from Indian telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) is unlikely to be relaunched this month, investment bankers said on Thursday.

The $650 million to $800 million jumbo offering of global depositary receipts (GDRs) -- India's biggest ever -- is awaiting approval from the government. Newspapers have speculated that the issue may be launched in September.
This would be the state-run firm's third launch attempt in two years. The first two attempts in 1994 were unsuccessful.
Global co-ordinators to the issue Kleinwort Benson, Jardine Fleming and Salomon Brothers were tightlipped on details about the issue.

"You've got a whole conflicting spectrum of market rumours about the issue and it's clear there are very inconsistent messages coming through about VSNL," said a spokesman for one of the co-ordinators, declining to give any details.
An investment banker close to the issue managers said the likelihood of government approval was "fairly positive."
But investment bankers said VSNL was unlikely to launch its issue in the same month as a much-awaited $400 million GDR offering from India's largest commercial bank, the State Bank of India (SBI).
SBI is due to begin pre-marketing for its GDR on September 16 with roadshows scheduled around September 23.
"There have never been two mega issues from India in the same month, even in better market conditions," one investment banker said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange has lost 550 points or nearly 14 percent from the year's peak of 4,069 on June 18.
